questions.cardText:
[History] The ancient civilization of Mesopotamia was located in the modern-day region of:
A. Iraq B. Egypt C. Israel
Answer: A.
questions.de: Dem Gebiet welches heutigen Staates entspricht das antike Mesopotamien ungefähr?
questions.en: The territory of which modern country corresponds roughly to ancient Mesopotamia?

timeline.labelEn: Sumerians and Akkadians dominate Mesopotamia, from the start of recorded history to the fall of Babylon
timeline.labelDe: Sumerer und Akkader beherrschen Mesopotamien, vom Beginn der Schriftgeschichte bis zum Fall Babylons

questions.notes: In the broader sense Mesopotamia also includes parts of southwestern Iran, southeastern Turkey, northeastern Syria and Kuwait.

questions.cardText:
[Zoology] Why can many birds stand on ice or snow barefoot without getting frostbite?
A. Their feet are insulated with a special coating
B. They shiver to heat up their feet
C. Their feet are already close to the temperature of the ice
Answer: C. Birds living in cold climates can maintain their feet just warm enough to avoid frostbite, and their circulation is fast enough that blood does not stay in the feet long enough to freeze. In severe cold, they may stand on one foot, tucking the other under their feathers to further reduce heat loss.
questions.de: Welches Blutgefäßgeflecht in den Beinen ermöglicht vielen Vögeln, auf Eis zu stehen, indem es die Füße per Gegenstrom-Wärmetausch nahe der Umgebungstemperatur hält?
questions.en: What network of blood vessels in their legs lets many birds stand on ice by keeping their feet close to the surrounding temperature through countercurrent heat exchange?

timeline.labelEn: Galen coins the term rete mirabile (“wonderful net”)
timeline.labelDe: Galen prägt den Begriff Rete mirabile („Wundernetz“)

questions.notes: The card's answer (feet already close to the ice's temperature) is right; the mechanism is countercurrent heat exchange in the retia mirabilia of the legs, so 'countercurrent heat exchange' is also accepted.
